subject.title: fix(gateway): avoid stale wake delays after node re-pairing

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this broad persistent pairing-generation authorization boundary across gateway runtime state, or should the work be reduced to a narrowly scoped stale wake-state repair?
rationale: The patch changes the trust boundary for authenticated node sessions and durable pairing state across 79 files; source snippets show a coherent direction, but choosing the permanent authorization model and blast radius requires gateway-owner intent.

options.title: Endorse the unified generation boundary
options.body: Keep the cross-layer design and require exact-head check resolution plus gateway-owner confirmation that all node-owned lifecycle paths should be fenced this way.

options.title: Narrow to wake-state cleanup
options.body: Retain only the removal/re-pair wake, nudge, and pending-work cleanup needed for the reported failure, leaving broader session-generation authorization for a separately sponsored design.

recommendation.title: Endorse the unified generation boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the cross-layer design and require exact-head check resolution plus gateway-owner confirmation that all node-owned lifecycle paths should be fenced this way.

likelyOwner.reason: A named historical owner could not be established safely from the supplied context, but the decision belongs with the current gateway-area owner rather than the contributor alone.
